[P3] 贝贝熊系列丛书
The Berenstain Bears

GET THE GIMMIES
（美）斯坦·博丹 简·博丹 绘著
Stan & Jan Berenstain

[P4] 贝贝熊一家住在熊王国的一座大树屋里，门前有一条金色的土路。小熊哥哥和小熊妹妹深爱着他们的爸爸、妈妈。当然，熊爸爸、熊妈妈也很疼爱孩子们。为了孩子，他们愿意付出一切。

但有时候，他们过于宠爱孩子，给孩子们买太多的好东西和玩具，在购物中心，让孩子们在摇摆鸭上骑个不停。

[P5] 或许就是这样，小熊哥哥和小熊妹妹养成了见啥要啥的习惯。或许也是因为，无论在超市、购物中心，还是在电视里，到处都可以见到新奇的东西、好玩的玩具和有趣的游戏，这对孩子们的诱惑实在是太大了。

总之，不知从什么时候开始，他们一见好东西就要，不给，就又哭又闹——尤其是经过超市的收银处时，那儿摆放着成堆的糖果和其他的好东西。

这一天，贝贝熊一家正排队等着结账，熊妈妈看到孩子们又盯着糖果，眼睛发亮，便说：“别看了，孩子们！咱们可不能一见到糖果架，就要买这买那，我可受不了！”

[P6] 糖果
小熊妹妹呼呼唧唧地说："妈妈，可那儿有口香糖球儿，我最喜欢吃啦！"
"还有我最爱吃的香槟口香糖！"小熊哥哥也小声嘀咕着。
熊妈妈说："别说了，我不想听！"
熊爸爸笑着说："得了，咱们也是从孩子过来的。"说着，把孩子想要的东西递给了他们。

他们走出超市，熊妈妈说："这话不假，咱们也是从孩子过来的。但是，好习惯应该从小培养。我当然想……"
"看！看！新玩具！"小熊妹妹大声喊。
小熊哥哥也叫了起来："瞧，一只摇摆蛙！比摇摆鸭更棒！让我们骑骑吧，好吗？好吗？求求你们了！"

[P7] 熊爸爸刚给孩子们买了口香糖，觉得他们该满足了。可是，见他们这样恳求，他叹了口气，只好从口袋掏出钱来，塞进投币口。

他看了看熊妈妈，耸耸肩说：“孩子毕竟是孩子嘛！”

[P8] 熊妈妈说：“话是不错，孩子毕竟是孩子，但也不能因为这样，每次看到想要的东西，就又蹦又跳，大哭大闹……”说着，穿过停车场，向自己家的车走去。

这时，孩子们又喊了起来：“看！快看！橡皮小猫！用手一捏，就伸舌头！”
熊妈妈说：“孩子们，够了！别再说了……”

[P9] 他们央求道：“给我们买嘛！买嘛！求求你们了。”
熊爸爸决定，该好好管管他们了。

熊爸爸提高了嗓门喊：“不许闹！”可孩子们只顾大喊大叫，根本就没听见他的话。小熊妹妹使劲地又蹦又跳，一下子摔了个四脚朝天，双脚在空中乱蹬。
“爱嘛！爱嘛！”孩子们大声喊着。停车场上所有的人都注意到了。

“那……”熊爸爸尴尬极了，只好对卖玩具的小贩说：
“就来两只橡皮小猫吧！”

[P10] 回到家，熊妈妈还在生气，熊爸爸肺都快气炸了，半晌说不出话来。孩子们开始忙自己的事，熊妈妈也沏好了一壶茶。这时，熊爸爸的怒气像火山一样喷发了出来：
“这太不像话了！太丢人了！太尴尬了！从没见过这么自私、贪心的孩子！太贪得无厌了！”
橡皮小猫不仅一捏就伸舌头，还会“吱吱”叫！就这样一路“吱吱吱”地回到家。

[P11] 熊妈妈平静地喝着茶，说：“这倒是，但静下来想想，他们为什么会见啥要啥？养成这个坏毛病，也许并不只是他们的错。咱们也有责任，咱们一直太顺着他们了。”
熊爸爸静静地听着，说：“也许你是对的。”
熊妈妈继续说：“咱们得跟孩子们好好谈谈，让他们明白，再不能见啥要啥了。”
熊爸爸把孩子们叫过来，告诉他们，自私、贪心、见啥要啥是不对的。
他解释说：“自私、贪心的孩子永远也不会快乐，因为不可能想要什么就有什么，生活就是这样，懂了吗？”
孩子们说：“爸爸，我们懂了。”

[P12] 熊爸爸告诉孩子们要懂得满足，也就是要享受已经拥有的，而不能见啥要啥，没完没了。
他又问："你们觉得对吗？"
孩子们说："爸爸，对极了！"
这时，他们听到了熟悉的关车门声，爷爷和奶奶来了！

小熊哥哥和小熊妹妹跑去开门，爷爷、奶奶刚走上台阶，他们又喊叫起来：
"带什么来啦？快说！带什么来啦？"他们的老毛病又犯了。

[P13] “回屋去！”熊爸爸咆哮起来，“回屋去！一星期不准看电视，不准要东西！一个月也不准！一年也不准！”
孩子们知道，现在不是争辩的时候，他们乖乖地赶紧上楼，溜进房间。

奶奶说：“我们好像来得不是时候。”
爷爷问：“我们带来的东西怎么办？给小熊哥哥的一个智力玩具，给小熊妹妹的一个陀螺。”
熊妈妈说：“你们的礼物要暂时放一放，这俩孩子已经养成见啥要啥的坏习惯了。”
熊爸爸补充说：“从没见过像他们两个这样贪得无厌的孩子，太不像话了！”

孩子们悄悄地把门打开了一条缝，听着。

[P14] 爷爷看着熊爸爸，说："从没见过！你小时候也是一个见啥要啥的孩子！"
小熊哥哥和小熊妹妹蹑手蹑脚地走到楼梯口，他们就能听得更清楚了。
熊爸爸问："我也是？"
"当然，那时还没有购物中心和超市，但有一个灰熊杂货店，那可真是个好地方！什么都有——蜂蜜蛋糕、甘草根、蜜糖苹果……还有各式各样的玩具和新奇的东西。你那时不也是见啥要啥吗？你啥都想要，太丢人了！我们都不好意思再去那儿买东西了！"

[P15] “后来，我们想出了一个办法。”奶奶说，“去商店前，我们让你想好要什么东西，可以是一块糖、一个玩具、一本书，每次只能要一样。”
“对！”爷爷说，“如果你又见啥要啥，我们就立刻回家，你什么都得不到。”
熊妈妈说：“这主意不错！”
熊爸爸说：“好！”，
孩子们踮着脚尖，悄悄溜回房间。
他们也觉得这个办法不错。

[P16] 贝贝熊一家又去了超市。这一次，他们
试了试爷爷、奶奶的办法，还真灵！

[P17] 这时，他们听到一个熟悉的声音：在他们身后的收银处，一个小孩正哭闹着要东西，在地上撒泼打滚，又踢又叫，
小熊妹妹说：“太讨厌、太丢人、太不像话了！咱们走吧？”

The Berenstain Bears and
GOT THE GIMMIES

When a cub's behavior takes a turn for the worst,
it's hard for parents to know what to do first.

1. Of course, the members of the Bear family, who lived in the big tree house down a sunny dirt road in Bear Country, loved each other. They loved each other very much. Brother and Sister Bear loved their mama and papa. Naturally, Mama and Papa Bear loved their cubs, and, of course, they were nice to them—as nice as they could be.

But sometimes, sometimes they were a little too nice. Sometimes the cubs got too many treats, too many toys, and too many rides on the Bucking Duck at the mall.

2. Maybe that's why Brother and Sister Bear got the gimmies. Or maybe it was because there were treats, toys, and fun things to do wherever they looked—at the supermarket, at the mall, on TV, and just about every whin-where.

Maybe that was why they began making a fuss to get what they wanted—especially at the supermarket checkout, where there were always stacks and stacks of candy and other goodies.

"Now, cubs," Mama bear said as the family got into the checkout line and she saw that old gimmie gleam in their eyes, "we can't have a big fuss every time we pass candy. I simply won't stand for it."

"But, Mama," whined Sister. "They have Gummy Gumballs! My favorite!"

"And Chewy Chompers! My favorite!" whined Brother.

"Now, hush!" said Mama. "I simply won't listen to another word..."

That's when Papa Bear smiled and said, "Now, Mama, you're only young once," and handed the cubs their favorite treats.

"It's only too true," said Mama as they were leaving the supermarket, "that you're only young once. But that's all the more reason to learn proper behavior while you're still young, and I certainly think—"

"Look! Look!" shouted Sister. "A new ride!"

15

[P19] “Hey, a Bucking Frog!” shouted Brother. “That looks even better than the Bucking Duck! May we ride it, please? May we? May we? Please!”
4. Now, Papa had just bought them treats, and he thought that was enough for one day. But the cubs made such a fuss that he sighed, dug into his pocket, and put some money in the slot.
Papa looked at Mama and shrugged. “Cubs will be cubs,” he said.
5. “It may be true that cubs will be cubs,” said Mama as they walked across the parking lot to their car.
“But that’s no excuse for jumping up and down and making a scene every time they see something they want—”
“Look! Look!” shouted the cubs once again. “Little rubber cats that stick out their tongues when you squeeze them!”
“Cubs,” said Mama, “that will be quite enough! I don’t want to hear another word...”
6. “Oh please!” they shouted. “May we have them? Please! Please! Please!”
Papa decided it was time to stop it all the fussing.
“Stop that fussing!” he said in his loudest Papa Bear voice. But they were making such a commotion they didn’t even hear him. Sister was jumping up and down so hard that he fell over backward and started kicking his feet in the air.
“Please! Please!” shouted the cubs so loudly that the whole parking lot took notice.
“Er—” said embarrassed Papa to the toy seller, “two of those rubber pussycats, please.”
7. The rubber pussycats not only stuck out their tongues when you squeezed them, they went squeak-squeak as well. And they squeak-squeaked all the way home.
Mama was quite annoyed by the time they got back to the tree house, but Papa was so angry he could hardly speak. It wasn’t until the cubs had gone about their business and Mama had made a pot of tea that Papa’s voice came back loud and clear.
“Of all the outrageous, disgraceful, embarrassing behavior I have ever seen,” he roared, “that selfish, greedy performance by our cubs was the worst! Brother and Sister have the worst case of the galloping greedy gummies I’ve ever seen!”
8. “Yes,” said Mama, calmly sipping her tea. “But have you ever stopped to think about why they have the gummies? Perhaps their greedy behavior isn’t all their fault. Perhaps it’s partly your fault for giving in every time they make a fuss.”
Papa listened quietly. “Perhaps so,” he said.
“It’s up to us,” she continued, “to explain things to them—to help them understand why it’s important not to be greedy.”
Then Papa called the cubs in for a talking-to. He told them why it wasn’t a good idea to be selfish and greedy and want everything in sight.
“Selfish, greedy cubs,” he explained, “can never be happy, because you just can’t have everything you want all the time—life isn’t like that. Do you understand?”
“Oh yes, Papa. We understand,” they said.
9. He talked to them about “counting their blessings,” which meant enjoying the things they had instead of forever wanting more and more and more.
“Does that make sense to you?” he asked.
“Oh yes, Papa,” they said. “It makes a lot of sense.”
That’s when the cubs heard the sound of a familiar car door. It was Grizzly Gramps and Gran come to call.
Brother and Sister ran to open the front door, and as Gramps and Gran came up the steps, they made the biggest fuss yet.
“Whaja-bringme? Whaja-bringme? Whaja-bringme?!”
That did it.
10. “Up to your room!” roared Papa. “Up to your room and no TV or treats for a week! For a month! For a year!”
The cubs knew this wasn’t the time to argue. They scurried up the stairs and into their room.
“We seem to have come at a bad time!” said Gran.
“What about these things we brought with us?” asked Gramps. “A puzzle for Brother and a top for Sister?”
“Your presents will have to wait, Gramps,” answered Mama. “I’m afraid Brother and Sister have a bad case of the gummies.”
“The galloping greedy gummies,” added Papa. “The worst case I’ve ever seen.”

[P20] The cubs opened their door a crack to listen.
11. "The worst case, ya say?" said Gramps, looking Papa in the eye. "Seems to me you were quite a gimme-cub yourself when you were little."
Brother and Sister sneaked to the top of the stairs so they could hear better.
"I was?" said Papa.
"Of course, we didn't have malls or supermarkets back then. But there was old Rufe Grizzly's General Store. Wonderful place. Sold just about everything—honey cake, licorice sticks, molasses apples, and all sorts of toys and novelties. And did you ever have the gimmies! Did you ever! You wanted everything in sight. Downright embarrassing. Why, it got so bad we couldn't go there anymore."
12. "So we worked out a deal," said Gran. "When it came time for a trip to the General Store, we had you decide on a treat ahead of time. It could be a sweet, a toy, or a book—and that was it for the day."
"Right," said Gramps. "And if you came down with the gimmies, we went right home and you got nothing!"
"That sounds like a pretty good plan to me," said Mama.
"Me too," said Papa.
The cubs tiptoed back to their room. It sounded okay to them, too.
13. The next time the Bear family went to the supermarket, they tried the Gramps-and-Gran plan. And it worked!
Brother decided he would get a book about dinosaurs, and Sister wanted a new box of crayons.
Mama and Papa were very proud when they passed the candy rack without so much as a peep.
Brother and Sister were pretty proud of themselves, too.
14. But then they heard it: the familiar sound of a cub with a bad case of the gimmies. The kicking, screaming cub was just behind them in the checkout line. You never heard such a fuss.
"What outrageous, disgraceful, embarrassing behaviour!" said Sister. "May we leave?"
"Yeah," said Brother. "Let's get out of here."
15. And that's how Brother and Sister Bear got rid of a pretty bad case of the galloping greedy gimmies.

[P4] The Berenstain Bears family lives in a big treehouse in Bear Country, with a golden dirt road in front. Brother Bear and Sister Bear deeply love their dad and mom. Of course, Papa Bear and Mama Bear also love their children very much. For their children, they are willing to give everything.

But sometimes, they spoil their children too much, buying them too many nice things and toys. In the shopping center, they let the children ride the wobbly duck endlessly.

[P5] Perhaps this is how it happened: Brother Bear and Sister Bear developed a habit of wanting whatever they saw. Perhaps it's also because, whether in supermarkets, shopping malls, or on TV, they could always see new and exciting things, fun toys, and interesting games—temptations too strong for children to resist.

In short, at some point, they began to demand anything they saw, and if denied, they would cry and throw tantrums—especially when passing the checkout counter in the supermarket, where piles of candy and other treats were displayed.

One day, the Berenstain Bears family was waiting in line to check out. Mama Bear saw her children staring at the candy, their eyes shining, and said, "Stop looking, children! We can't buy this and that every time we see a candy display. I just can't take it!"

[P6] Candy
Little Sister Bear chattered excitedly, "Mom, look! There are gumballs over there, and I love them the most!"
"And my favorite, champagne-flavored gum!" Little Brother Bear whispered.
Bear Mom said, "Enough, I don't want to hear it!"
Bear Dad smiled and said, "Come on, we were kids once too." He then handed the children the things they wanted.

As they left the supermarket, Bear Mom said, "That's true, we were kids once too. But good habits should be cultivated from a young age. Of course, I want to..."
"Look! Look! New toys!" Little Sister Bear shouted loudly.
Little Brother Bear also called out, "Hey, a wobbling frog! It's better than the wobbling duck! Let us ride it, okay? Okay? Please, please!"

[P7] Bear Dad had just bought the kids some bubble gum and thought they should be satisfied. But seeing them beg so desperately, he sighed and took out money from his pocket, putting it into the coin slot.

He looked at Bear Mom and shrugged, saying, "After all, they're just kids!"

[P8] Bear Mom said, "It's true, children are children, but we can't let them jump and cry every time they see something they want..." She said, walking through the parking lot toward their car.

At that moment, the children shouted again, "Look! Look! Rubber cats! Squeeze them, and they stick out their tongues!"
Bear Mom said, "Children, enough! Stop it..."

[P9] They pleaded, "Buy it for us! Buy it! Please, we beg you!"
Bear Dad decided it was time to discipline them.

Bear Dad raised his voice, shouting, "Stop it!" But the children just kept screaming and shouting, completely ignoring him. Little Bear Sister jumped and bounced wildly, then fell flat on her back, kicking her legs in the air.
"Love it! Love it!" the children shouted loudly. Everyone in the parking lot noticed.

"Well..." Bear Dad was extremely embarrassed, so he turned to the toy vendor and said,
"Just two rubber cats, please!"

[P10] When they got home, Mama Bear was still angry, and Papa Bear was so furious his lungs felt like they were about to explode. He couldn't speak for a while. The children started doing their own things, and Mama Bear had already brewed a pot of tea. At that moment, Papa Bear's anger erupted like a volcano:
"This is unacceptable! So embarrassing! So shameful! I've never seen such selfish, greedy children! So greedy and insatiable!"
The rubber cats not only stuck out their tongues when squeezed, but also made a "squeak squeak" sound! They made their way home with a continuous "squeak squeak squeak!"

[P11] Bear Mom calmly sipped her tea and said, "That's true. But if we think about it, why do they always want whatever they see? Developing this bad habit may not be entirely their fault. We also share responsibility—we've been too indulgent with them all along." 
Bear Dad listened quietly and said, "Maybe you're right." 
Bear Mom continued, "We need to have a serious talk with the children and help them understand that they can't always want whatever they see." 
Bear Dad called the children over and told them that being selfish, greedy, and always wanting everything was wrong. 
He explained, "Selfish, greedy children will never be happy, because they can't always get whatever they want. Life is like that, understand?" 
The children said, "Dad, we understand."

[P12] Bear Dad told the children to learn to be content, meaning to enjoy what they already have, and not to want everything they see, endlessly.
He then asked, "Do you think that's right?"
The children said, "Dad, absolutely!"
At that moment, they heard the familiar sound of car doors closing—Grandpa and Grandma had arrived!

Little Bear Brother and Little Bear Sister ran to open the door. As Grandpa and Grandma stepped onto the porch, they shouted again:
"What did you bring? Hurry up! What did you bring?" Their old habit was back.

[P13] "Go back to your room!" Bear Dad roared, "Go back to your room! No TV for a week, no asking for things! Not for a month! Not for a year!"

The children knew it wasn't the time to argue. They quietly hurried upstairs and slipped into their room.

Grandma said, "We seem to have come at a bad time."
Grandpa asked, "What should we do with the things we brought? A puzzle toy for little Bear Brother, a spinning top for little Bear Sister."
Bear Mom said, "Your gifts will have to wait. These two children have already developed the bad habit of wanting whatever they see."
Bear Dad added, "I've never seen such greedy children. It's disgraceful!"

The children quietly opened the door a crack and listened.

[P14] Grandpa looked at Bear Dad and said, "Never seen it! You were a child who wanted everything you saw when you were young!"
Little Bear Brother and Little Bear Sister crept quietly to the stairway, where they could hear better.
Bear Dad asked, "Me too?"
"Of course! Back then, there were no shopping malls or supermarkets, but there was a Grizzly General Store. It was such a great place! Everything was there—honey cakes, licorice roots, candy apples... and all kinds of toys and novelties. Weren't you always wanting everything you saw back then? You wanted everything, it was so embarrassing! We were too ashamed to go back there to buy things!"

[P15] "Later, we came up with an idea," Grandma said. "Before going to the store, we'll let you decide what you want—maybe a candy, a toy, or a book—but only one thing each time." 
"Right!" Grandpa said. "If you start wanting everything again, we'll go home right away, and you won't get anything." 
Bear Mom said, "That's a good idea!" 
Bear Dad said, "Okay!" 

The children tiptoed quietly back to their room. 
They thought this idea was pretty good too.

GOT THE GIMMIES

When a cub's behavior takes a turn for the worst,
it's hard for parents to know what to do first.

1. Of course, the members of the Bear family, who lived in the big tree house down a sunny dirt road in Bear Country, loved each other. They loved each other very much. Brother and Sister Bear loved their mama and papa. Naturally, Mama and Papa Bear loved their cubs, and, of course, they were nice to them—as nice as they could be.

But sometimes, sometimes they were a little too nice. Sometimes the cubs got too many treats, too many toys, and too many rides on the Bucking Duck at the mall.

2. Maybe that's why Brother and Sister Bear got the gimmies. Or maybe it was because there were treats, toys, and fun things to do wherever they looked—at the supermarket, at the mall, on TV, and just about every whin-where.

Maybe that was why they began making a fuss to get what they wanted—especially at the supermarket checkout, where there were always stacks and stacks of candy and other goodies.

"Now, cubs," Mama bear said as the family got into the checkout line and she saw that old gimmie gleam in their eyes, "we can't have a big fuss every time we pass candy. I simply won't stand for it."

"But, Mama," whined Sister. "They have Gummy Gumballs! My favorite!"

"And Chewy Chompers! My favorite!" whined Brother.

"Now, hush!" said Mama. "I simply won't listen to another word..."

That's when Papa Bear smiled and said, "Now, Mama, you're only young once," and handed the cubs their favorite treats.

"It's only too true," said Mama as they were leaving the supermarket, "that you're only young once. But that's all the more reason to learn proper behavior while you're still young, and I certainly think—"

"Look! Look!" shouted Sister. "A new ride!"

15

[P19] "Hey, a Bucking Frog!" shouted Brother. "That looks even better than the Bucking Duck! May we ride it, please? May we? May we? Please!"
4. Now, Papa had just bought them treats, and he thought that was enough for one day. But the cubs made such a fuss that he sighed, dug into his pocket, and put some money in the slot.
Papa looked at Mama and shrugged. "Cubs will be cubs," he said.
5. "It may be true that cubs will be cubs," said Mama as they walked across the parking lot to their car.
"But that’s no excuse for jumping up and down and making a scene every time they see something they want—"
"Look! Look!" shouted the cubs once again. "Little rubber cats that stick out their tongues when you squeeze them!"
"Cubs," said Mama, "that will be quite enough! I don’t want to hear another word..."
6. "Oh please!" they shouted. "May we have them? Please! Please! Please!"
Papa decided it was time to stop it all the fussing.
"Stop that fussing!" he said in his loudest Papa Bear voice. But they were making such a commotion they didn’t even hear him. Sister was jumping up and down so hard that he fell over backward and started kicking his feet in the air.
"Please! Please!" shouted the cubs so loudly that the whole parking lot took notice.
"Er—" said embarrassed Papa to the toy seller, "two of those rubber pussycats, please."
7. The rubber pussycats not only stuck out their tongues when you squeezed them, they went squeak-squeak as well. And they squeak-squeaked all the way home.
Mama was quite annoyed by the time they got back to the tree house, but Papa was so angry he could hardly speak. It wasn’t until the cubs had gone about their business and Mama had made a pot of tea that Papa’s voice came back loud and clear.
"Of all the outrageous, disgraceful, embarrassing behavior I have ever seen," he roared, "that selfish, greedy performance by our cubs was the worst! Brother and Sister have the worst case of the galloping greedy gummies I’ve ever seen!"
8. "Yes," said Mama, calmly sipping her tea. "But have you ever stopped to think about why they have the gummies? Perhaps their greedy behavior isn’t all their fault. Perhaps it’s partly your fault for giving in every time they make a fuss."
Papa listened quietly. "Perhaps so," he said.
"It’s up to us," she continued, "to explain things to them—to help them understand why it’s important not to be greedy."
Then Papa called the cubs in for a talking-to. He told them why it wasn’t a good idea to be selfish and greedy and want everything in sight.
"Selfish, greedy cubs," he explained, "can never be happy, because you just can’t have everything you want all the time—life isn’t like that. Do you understand?"
"Oh yes, Papa. We understand," they said.
9. He talked to them about "counting their blessings," which meant enjoying the things they had instead of forever wanting more and more and more.
"Does that make sense to you?" he asked.
"Oh yes, Papa," they said. "It makes a lot of sense."
That’s when the cubs heard the sound of a familiar car door. It was Grizzly Gramps and Gran come to call.
Brother and Sister ran to open the front door, and as Gramps and Gran came up the steps, they made the biggest fuss yet.
"Whaja-bringme? Whaja-bringme? Whaja-bringme?!"
That did it.
10. "Up to your room!" roared Papa. "Up to your room and no TV or treats for a week! For a month! For a year!"
The cubs knew this wasn’t the time to argue. They scurried up the stairs and into their room.
"We seem to have come at a bad time!" said Gran.
"What about these things we brought with us?" asked Gramps. "A puzzle for Brother and a top for Sister?"
"Your presents will have to wait, Gramps," answered Mama. "I’m afraid Brother and Sister have a bad case of the gummies."
"The galloping greedy gummies," added Papa. "The worst case I’ve ever seen."

[P20] The cubs opened their door a crack to listen.
11. "The worst case, ya say?" said Gramps, looking Papa in the eye. "Seems to me you were quite a gimme-cub yourself when you were little."
Brother and Sister sneaked to the top of the stairs so they could hear better.
"I was?" said Papa.
"Of course, we didn't have malls or supermarkets back then. But there was old Rufe Grizzly's General Store. Wonderful place. Sold just about everything—honey cake, licorice sticks, molasses apples, and all sorts of toys and novelties. And did you ever have the gimmies! Did you ever! You wanted everything in sight. Downright embarrassing. Why, it got so bad we couldn't go there anymore."
12. "So we worked out a deal," said Gran. "When it came time for a trip to the General Store, we had you decide on a treat ahead of time. It could be a sweet, a toy, or a book—and that was it for the day."
"Right," said Gramps. "And if you came down with the gimmies, we went right home and you got nothing!"
"That sounds like a pretty good plan to me," said Mama.
"Me too," said Papa.
The cubs tiptoed back to their room. It sounded okay to them, too.
13. The next time the Bear family went to the supermarket, they tried the Gramps-and-Gran plan. And it worked!
Brother decided he would get a book about dinosaurs, and Sister wanted a new box of crayons.
Mama and Papa were very proud when they passed the candy rack without so much as a peep.
Brother and Sister were pretty proud of themselves, too.
14. But then they heard it: the familiar sound of a cub with a bad case of the gimmies. The kicking, screaming cub was just behind them in the checkout line. You never heard such a fuss.
"What outrageous, disgraceful, embarrassing behaviour!" said Sister. "May we leave?"
"Yeah," said Brother. "Let's get out of here."
15. And that's how Brother and Sister Bear got rid of a pretty bad case of the galloping greedy gimmies.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《见啥要啥》的封面，展示了贝贝熊一家在超市购物的场景，小熊们表现出对商品的强烈欲望，封面包含书名、作者、译者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页为绘本《见啥要啥》的目录页和扉页，左侧列出了贝贝熊系列丛书1-30册的书名及英文标题，右侧为本书书名、副标题及插图，插图展示了一家三口在超市购物的场景，强调了孩子有坏毛病时父母应如何应对的主题。
[P3] 本页为绘本《见啥要啥》的扉页，左侧插图展示两只小熊在众多玩具和糖果中兴奋跳跃，右侧为书名、作者、译者及出版社信息，并强调亲子共读与共同成长的主题。
[P4] 本页介绍了贝贝熊一家的生活背景，强调了父母对孩子的深爱，同时也指出他们有时会过度宠爱孩子，例如在购物中心给孩子买太多东西并让他们骑摇摆鸭。
[P5] 本页通过文字和插图解释了小熊兄妹养成‘见啥要啥’习惯的原因，并描绘了他们在超市收银处面对糖果时的诱惑，以及熊妈妈对此的担忧和无奈。
[P6] 本页描绘了贝贝熊兄妹在超市糖果区的诱惑以及父母的无奈妥协，随后走出超市后，熊妈妈意识到应从小培养好习惯，但孩子们立刻被新玩具吸引，再次提出要求。
[P7] 熊爸爸在超市为孩子们买了口香糖，但孩子们仍继续恳求，他最终无奈地投币让孩子们骑上摇摆玩具；他向熊妈妈解释，认为孩子毕竟是孩子，需要宽容。
[P8] 熊妈妈在停车场对孩子们的无理取闹表示无奈，正准备离开时，孩子们又被路边摊的橡皮小猫吸引，再次吵闹着要买，熊妈妈再次劝阻。
[P9] 贝贝熊兄妹在停车场再次吵闹着要买玩具，熊爸爸试图管教但无效，最终无奈妥协，为他们买了两只橡皮小猫。
[P10] 贝贝熊一家开车回家，熊爸爸因孩子们在超市和停车场的无理要求而愤怒爆发，熊妈妈在一旁无奈，孩子们则兴奋地玩着新买的橡皮小猫。
[P11] 熊妈妈和熊爸爸反思了孩子们‘见啥要啥’习惯的成因，并决定与孩子们沟通。熊爸爸向孩子们解释自私和贪心的坏处，孩子们表示理解。
[P12] 熊爸爸教导孩子们要懂得满足，孩子们表示赞同。但当爷爷奶奶到来时，他们立刻又表现出‘见啥要啥’的老毛病，吵着要问带来了什么礼物。
[P13] 熊爸爸因孩子们的无理要求而愤怒，禁止他们看电视和要东西，孩子们只好上楼。爷爷奶奶来访，熊妈妈和熊爸爸表示孩子们已养成见啥要啥的坏习惯，决定暂不给礼物，孩子们则悄悄在门后偷听。
[P14] 爷爷向熊爸爸讲述自己小时候也和孩子们一样见啥要啥，回忆起当年在灰熊杂货店时的贪心行为，熊爸爸对此感到惊讶，而小熊兄妹则悄悄在楼梯口偷听。
[P15] 爷爷奶奶向熊爸爸和熊妈妈提议，在去商店前让孩子提前决定只买一样东西，否则就回家不买，熊爸爸和熊妈妈同意了。孩子们在楼梯口偷听到后，觉得这个办法不错，悄悄溜回房间。
[P16] 贝贝熊一家去超市购物，孩子们按照爷爷奶奶的建议，只选了一样东西，路过糖果架时没有多看，父母为此感到骄傲。
[P17] 在超市收银处，一个小孩因想要东西而哭闹打滚，小熊兄妹看到后觉得丢人，决定离开。
[P18] 本页展示了贝贝熊一家在超市购物的场景，孩子们在收银台前因想买糖果而吵闹，但最终在父母的引导下改掉了见啥要啥的坏毛病。页面文字为故事的英文原文及中文总结。
[P19] 本页描述了贝贝熊兄妹在超市因想要玩具而吵闹，父母最终妥协购买后，回家后因持续吵闹而被父亲严厉训斥。随后，爷爷奶奶来访，孩子们再次因想得到礼物而大吵大闹，父亲因此命令他们回房间反省，并禁止看电视和吃零食，父母反思了自己对孩子的纵容行为。
[P20] 本页讲述了贝贝熊兄妹在偷听到爷爷奶奶的购物规则后，决定遵守并成功在超市只选一样东西，感到自豪。但当他们看到另一个孩子因贪心而大哭大闹时，感到尴尬并选择离开，最终成功改掉了贪心的坏习惯。
